item.text:
**Verdict**  
Mixed, leaning somewhat positive on economic-shock relief, but weak on broad crisis-suffering reduction across disasters, displacement, and protection failures.

**Positive**
- [Pakistan: IMF Reaches Agreement on Economic Policies for 37-month EFF](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff) | IMF | 2024-07-12 | The program explicitly tied policy to disinflation, flexible exchange rates, targeted subsidies through BISP, and energy-cost reforms. That is direct evidence of using policy tools to reduce suffering from the macro shock environment. | IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `5B.9`
- [Pakistan: World Bank Approves $535 Million for Crisis-Resilient Social Protection and Climate-Smart Growth](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/20/pakistan-world-bank-approves-535-million-for-crisis-resilient-social-protection-and-climate-smart-growth-in-the-livestoc) | World Bank | 2024-06-20 | The Bank said Pakistan was strengthening social protection for poor and vulnerable households to absorb climate and economic shocks, with support for female farmers and food security. This is strong positive evidence on reducing avoidable suffering from shocks. | IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`
- [Pakistan renegotiating power deals to cut costs, minister says](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/pakistan-renegotiating-power-deals-to-cut-costs-minister-says-3606192) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-07 | The government renegotiated expensive power contracts because energy prices were hurting households and firms. This is a concrete shock-response that likely reduced some avoidable economic pain. | IDs: `6B.6`, `5B.9`, `6B.2`
- [PM for collective efforts to eliminate menace of terrorism](https://www.radio.gov.pk/22-06-2024/pm-for-collective-efforts-to-eliminate-menace-of-terrorism) | Radio Pakistan | 2024-06-22 | Sharif launched a national counterterrorism campaign with provincial consensus and resources for the armed forces. That is not a broad humanitarian program, but it is a real attempt to reduce suffering from violent insecurity. | IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.1`

**Negative**
- [Pakistan implementing an ambitious, credible and clearly communicated economic reform plan critical for robust recovery](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/01/pakistan-implementing-an-ambitious-credible-and-clearly-communicated-economic-reform-plan-critical-for-robust-recovery-p) | World Bank | 2024-04-02 | The World Bank said growth was expected to be only 1.8 percent, poverty was still around 40 percent, and reserves/import constraints were still binding. That is strong counterevidence that suffering had not yet been broadly reduced early in 2024. | IDs: `6B.6`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`
- [Reform implementation remains critical for continued economic recovery and poverty reduction](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank) | World Bank | 2024-10-10 | Growth recovered, but poverty still rose to 40.5 percent. That undercuts any claim that 2024 delivered broad relief to households in a crisis setting. | IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.2`, `5B.10`
- [Pakistan widening crackdown on dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | HRW said the government clamped down on dissent and that weak social security jeopardized rights to health, food, and an adequate standard of living, including vulnerable migrants. This weighs against a welfare-first crisis response. | IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.1`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`
- [Pakistan abusive evictions target urban poor](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/28/pakistan-abusive-evictions-target-urban-poor) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-28 | Authorities forcibly evicted low-income residents, shop owners, and street vendors without adequate notice, compensation, or resettlement. That is direct negative evidence on avoiding avoidable suffering during an economic and housing shock. | IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`
- [End escalating attacks on minority Ahmadiyya community](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-21 | Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests, harassment, and blocked religious rites for Ahmadis while authorities failed to ensure safety. This shows a failure to protect a vulnerable group during an ongoing civic-security crisis. | IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.3`, `6B.1`
- [Urgent and transparent investigation needed into deadly crackdown on opposition protesters](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/urgent-and-transparent-investigation-needed-into-deadly-crackdown-on-opposition-protesters/) | Amnesty International | 2024-11-27 | Amnesty described deaths, mass detentions, and a communications blackout during the Islamabad crackdown. That is direct evidence against reducing avoidable suffering in a domestic crisis. | IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.1`, `6B.3`

**Search Gap**
- I found solid evidence for economic-shock mitigation and some social-protection scaling, but not strong 2024 evidence of major pandemic, famine, or disaster-relief management by Sharif personally.
- The record is much better on macro stabilization and targeted safety nets than on transparent, large-scale crisis humanitarian delivery.
